audit.summary: The Lean file states that Mathlib's riemannZeta has no zero with real part > 7/8, i.e., the quasi-Riemann hypothesis with σ₀ = 7/8 for ζ. The statement is faithful to the ζ part of the paper's Theorem, but it covers only ζ (not Dirichlet or Hecke L-functions), and the proof is `sorry`.

glossary.plain: Mathlib's Riemann zeta function ζ(s), the meromorphic continuation to ℂ (with the junk value at s = 1)
glossary.note: At s=1 Mathlib assigns a junk value, but s=1 has real part 1 > 7/8 and the value there is nonzero (γ-related), so the theorem is still true and is not weakened by this.

glossary.plain: For every complex s with Re s > 7/8, ζ(s) ≠ 0.
glossary.standard_concept: Zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for ζ

lean_claims.plain: For all s ∈ ℂ with Re s > 7/8, riemannZeta s ≠ 0.

paper_claims.plain: Every finite-order Hecke L-function over Q(√-3) has no zero in Re s > 7/8; the same holds for every Dirichlet L-function, including ζ(s); a pole at s=1 for principal characters is allowed.

coverage.why: The ζ instance of the zero-free region Re s > 7/8 is exactly stated.
No statement about general Dirichlet characters.

flags.explanation: Only the ζ case is formalized; the Dirichlet L-function and Hecke L-function over Q(√-3) claims are not covered. The ζ case is the quasi-RH highlighted in the paper.
flags.probe_idea: State for all q and Dirichlet characters χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q, with Re s > 7/8 and (χ ≠ 1 ∨ s ≠ 1), DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s ≠ 0.

lint_verdicts.why: (7/8 : ℝ) is real-typed division of numerals, which evaluates to 0.875 as intended.
